set.body:
Journey: Bring in. Owner task.

Outcome
We know what the legacy XNAT holds, and one study is chosen to migrate first.

Acceptance
1. Facts recorded as a note on this item: XNAT version; how a service account signs in; whether scans are stored as DICOM, NIfTI or both; number of projects, subjects and sessions; total size; whether scanners still send to it.
2. One first study is named. Guide: MRI with at least T1w and BOLD; 20 to 60 participants; under 10,000 files and folders after conversion and under 32 MiB of JSON sidecars in total, which are the current limits for one release; an ethics protocol that permits de-identified use inside the institute; ideally from the owner's own lab.
3. A read-only XNAT account exists for the migration tool. Its credentials are stored outside the repository and the tracker.
4. The list of the study's distinct series descriptions (from the XNAT interface, or from xnat2bids scan once IN2 exists) is handed to IN3 for the mapping.

Fallback
If no real study is cleared by 11 December, IN6 runs against a public DICOM study loaded into a throwaway XNAT container, and the real study follows.

Never put hostnames, credentials or participant identifiers in the tracker or the repository.
set.title: IN1: Survey the XNAT and choose the first study
